title: Civil Rights Cold Case Investigations Support Act of 2022
policy_area: Civil Rights and Liberties, Minority Issues
official_summary:
Civil Rights Cold Case Investigations Support Act of 2022

This act extends the Civil Rights Cold Case Records Review Board until 2026 (or 2027 if the board opts for an additional one-year extension). The board reviews the decisions of federal agencies to postpone the disclosure of civil rights cold case records (i.e., unsolved civil rights cases from 1940-1979).

summary.headline: This law extends the board that reviews federal decisions to hold back records about unsolved civil rights cases from 1940 to 1979.
summary.what_it_does: The Civil Rights Cold Case Records Review Board was set up to look at federal agency decisions to delay releasing records about unsolved civil rights cases from 1940 to 1979. This law extends the board's time to operate until 2026. The board can choose one more year, which would push the end date to 2027.

who_it_affects.group: Families and researchers seeking records on unsolved civil rights-era cases
who_it_affects.how: The board that reviews whether federal records can be withheld keeps working for several more years, so records requests can continue to be reviewed.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies that hold civil rights cold case records
who_it_affects.how: Their decisions to postpone releasing these records remain subject to review by the board for longer.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 5, 2022; the board's extended operation runs until 2026, or 2027 if the board opts for a one-year extension.
